sampling_model.design: Known independent unit-level \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment on a fixed partition into unequal disjoint cliques.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) units, partition, graph, exposure map, and all exposure-indexed potential outcomes are fixed.
sampling_model.treatment: Within block \(l\), All Treat and All Control are mutually exclusive events, each with probability \(q_l=2^{-r_l}\); blocks are independent.
sampling_model.overlap: Every target exposure has known positive probability \(q_l\), which may vary with \(l\) and vanish along triangular arrays.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No superpopulation nuisance is estimated; on a unanimous block, the observed block mean equals the corresponding fixed-schedule block mean, and omitted blocks receive deterministic bias protection.
sampling_model.randomness: The only inferential randomness is \(Z\), augmented by independent \(R\) solely to include externally randomized interval procedures in the decision class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Exposure-weighted estimators are unbiased, conservative randomization variances are available, and local-dependence conditions justify asymptotic normal intervals.

Section 4.3 constructs finite-sample Hoeffding-type confidence intervals for population-average direct, indirect, total, and overall effects of binary outcomes under a two-stage partial-interference design.

Exact confidence sets for binary direct, indirect, total, and overall effects under two-stage randomization and stratified partial interference are obtained by inversion of randomization tests, with a targeted approximation algorithm.
Full-neighborhood exposure probabilities can be exponentially small in degree and graph-cluster randomization can sharply reduce Horvitz--Thompson variance.
Conflict-graph connectivity controls upper and lower minimax mean-squared-error rates when the design and estimator are decision variables.
Under ordinary randomized experiments, nonasymptotic treatment-effect intervals attain the effective sample size \(n\pi\), with matching estimation-rate lower bounds.
Between-class moduli lower-bound expected confidence-interval length and ordered moduli yield procedures within constant factors in Gaussian models.
Convex regression classes admit finite-sample modulus-based optimal intervals and sharp efficiency bounds under normal errors with known variance.
Under interference, existence of unbiased estimators does not guarantee variance that decreases with population size.
Randomized fuzzy intervals attain a minimum expected-length benchmark for a one-parameter Bernoulli observation problem.

body.tldr: Unequal clique sizes turn full-neighborhood treatment and control exposure into independent nonidentical categorical reveals. The observed-data block Horvitz--Thompson estimator now has a fully derived clipped Bernstein interval, supported by a proved finite-product exponential lemma. The capped program has a certified water-filling optimizer and constant-factor trimming dual, and the trimmed observed-data interval gives the corresponding global upper bound. The exact hard-subexperiment embedding preserves all assignment ancillaries and arbitrary external interval randomization. The two all-procedure lower bounds remain open: the no-dominance tilted-sign posterior-spread lemma and the unrestricted smooth-location erasure lower bound. Consequently, the converse halves of the no-dominance frontier and the consistency boundary are not yet claimed. The pinned \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\) diagnostic separately reports graph rejection and package-versus-reference label mismatch.

project_justification.gap: Existing partial-interference confidence procedures do not lower-bound expected length over every measurable externally randomized interval under fixed balanced assignment on unequal cliques. The remaining mathematical gap is now sharply localized: a biased weighted-Rademacher posterior-spread theorem under no dominance, and a smooth-location erasure lower bound with moving-support endpoint control in the capped regime.
project_justification.niche: The paper treats the known assignment distribution as the sole source of randomness and exposes two computable design scales: the quadratic rare-exposure scale for the implementable Bernstein interval and the capped water-filling or trimming scale when a block dominates. The optimizer and the trimming comparison are certified; their all-procedure minimax lower interpretation remains a stated open question.
project_justification.fill: The proved portion consists of the exact independent categorical block reduction, an observed-data Horvitz--Thompson estimator, a finite-sample clipped Bernstein interval, a bias-protected trimmed interval, a KKT-certified capped water-filling optimizer, a constant-factor trimming dual, and an exact Markov-kernel embedding covering randomized procedures. Exact six-block and two-scale calculations remain diagnostics. The note does not promote either unresolved erasure posterior-spread argument to a theorem.

body.related_work: TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012, Section 4.3, derives finite-sample Hoeffding-type intervals for allocation-strategy effects under a two-stage partial-interference design, and RigdonHudgens2015 obtains exact confidence sets for those effects by randomization-test inversion. Those estimands and designs differ from the fixed unequal-clique All Treat versus All Control contrast here. AronowSamii2017 supplies the design--exposure--estimand architecture and exposure-specific inverse weighting, while UganderKarrerBackstromKleinberg2013 shows that full-neighborhood exposure probabilities may be exponentially small in degree. BasseAiroldi2018 gives a nonconcentration warning, UganderYin2023 changes the design to mitigate small probabilities, and KandirosHarshawSavje2026 studies design-based mean-squared-error criteria rather than all-interval confidence length. CaiLow2004 and ArmstrongKolesar2018 motivate modulus logic in Gaussian experiments, but do not prove the weighted nonidentical erasure posterior-spread result needed here. The present proved additions are self-contained finite-product concentration and capped-optimization or trimming certificates; neither is used as a substitute for the still-open randomized-interval lower bounds. The pinned \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\) source uses the complement of All Treat in its second output column, so the diagnostic compares it with an independently recomputed unanimous All Control reference.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The finite-product concentration lemma, clipped interval, trimmed upper interval, capped optimizer, and trimming dual are proved. The hard-subexperiment lemma also settles only the experiment-to-experiment bridge: it reconstructs unrevealed assignments and transfers coverage and expected length without discarding ancillaries. The no-dominance lower frontier still requires a biased weighted-Rademacher concentration-function bound carrying the exact conditional variance factors \(1-t^2s_l^2\), followed by posterior missed-mass calculations in both conditional-noise regimes. The unrestricted lower frontier separately requires a smooth-location erasure construction with explicit moving-support endpoint control and a justified likelihood or Hellinger-to-posterior-spread conversion. Until those arguments close, neither the two-sided minimax frontier nor the reverse implication in the consistency boundary is established.
body.honest_scope: The proved results concern fixed outcomes in \([-1/2,1/2]\), known unequal disjoint clique blocks, and independent unit-level \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment. The estimator and both upper intervals are measurable from \(D\) and known design quantities. The capped water-filling optimizer and its constant-factor relation to trimming are certified. Arbitrary external interval randomization is preserved by the exact lower-experiment embedding, but the required posterior-spread inequalities are still open. Therefore the no-dominance and unrestricted minimax lower bounds, the full consistency equivalence, and the two-sided equal- and two-scale rate corollaries remain unproved. The statement that \(S\to0\) is not necessary is nevertheless supported by an explicit valid clique triangular array and the proved trimmed upper bound. Overlapping or nonclique neighborhoods are rejected before the software diagnostic reports an interval.
